paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Everything God asks of us comes down to love. Jesus says, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind." (Matthew 22:37) Then He adds a second one that's like it: "Love your neighbor as yourself." (Matthew 22:39) And He says, "All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments." (Matthew 22:40)

So here's what that means for you. When you open the Word, don't treat it like a pile of random rules. Every page hangs on those two hooks. All of you loves God, and that love spills over onto the person next to you. I spent years in a drawer thinking I was only useful when somebody needed me, but love never works that way. It's for the person right in front of you, so go bake some love today, baker!

Then Jesus turns the tables and asks about the Christ. David, speaking in the Spirit, calls Him "Lord." (Matthew 22:43) So the Christ is David's son, and David's Lord too. That's the One we love with all of us. Nobody could answer Him a word (Matthew 22:46), but you don't have to stay quiet, friend. You get to know Him, trust Him and follow Him. The story isn't over, and neither is the teaching.
